query: How do review themes differ between positive and negative Yelp sentiment?

per_column.name: service_staff_conduct
per_column.rationale: Well-separated interpretable categories (friendly, rude, indifferent, unprofessional) capturing a distinct review theme that can be segmented and compared against sentiment.

per_column.name: food_quality_signal
per_column.rationale: Ordinal, human-readable quality scale (excellent to inedible) representing an external thematic dimension well-suited to cross-tabulation with label_pos.

per_column.name: food_praised_highlight
per_column.rationale: Interpretable categories of what food aspect is praised; a bit skewed toward not_present but still offers meaningful positive-theme segmentation.

per_column.name: atmosphere_ambiance_signal
per_column.rationale: Distinct ambiance theme with interpretable polarity categories; heavily dominated by not_present (197) which weakens comparison power but categories remain meaningful.

per_column.name: return_recommend_intent
per_column.rationale: Behavioral-intent categories (return yes/no, warn others) that are highly interpretable and strongly relatable to sentiment differences.

judge.rationale: All five columns are external, thematic, associational variables with well-separated, human-interpretable categories that directly enable grouping and comparison against positive/negative sentiment, exactly matching the query about review themes. None merely restate the label, and none are opaque scores. The main weakness is that several columns are dominated by a 'not_present' value (especially atmosphere and food_praised_highlight), which thins the comparison base for some categories, but the remaining categories are still informative and well-defined.
